Summary: Baseline current implementation and confirm scope
Description:
Objective: Record verified capabilities, limitations, stakeholders, assumptions, and prototype-versus-production boundaries.

Detail: Use repository modules, DDL, tests, Bundle, and dated run evidence to approve the first scope baseline. Do not describe proposed controls as deployed.

Inputs: Repository; product/operations contacts

Expected outputs: Approved scope and implementation inventory
Acceptance Criteria:
- Inventory covers all six workflow tasks, 10 physical tables, two notebooks, Bundle targets, and test evidence.
- Every capability is labelled implemented, partial, planned, or to be confirmed with a repository evidence reference.
- Business owner confirms prototype scope and named decision owners before Sprint 2 exit.

Summary: Approve business and functional requirements
Description:
Objective: Turn current capabilities and business needs into testable BR/FR acceptance criteria.

Detail: Confirm user roles, daily business outputs, timing, correction semantics, report needs, and sign-off owners. Link BR-001..008 to FR-001..013.

Inputs: Implementation inventory; business/operations interviews

Expected outputs: Signed requirements and acceptance criteria
Acceptance Criteria:
- All eight business requirements have an owner, priority, acceptance evidence, and dependency.
- All 13 functional requirements identify input, processing, output, business rule, and failure behavior.
- Product owner records decisions or explicit TBDs; no unsupported policy is silently assumed.

Summary: Set measurable non-functional and operational targets
Description:
Objective: Agree performance, availability, support, security, retention, RTO/RPO, and recovery targets.

Detail: Use proposed thresholds as discussion points only. Confirm owner, measurement window, and evidence for each target.

Inputs: Business/technology policy owners; proposed NFRs

Expected outputs: Approved NFR baseline
Acceptance Criteria:
- NFR-01..10 each has a confirmed target or named owner and due date for TBD.
- Performance baseline includes representative row counts, symbols, runtime, and cost.
- Retention, access classification, RTO/RPO, support hours, and alert response are approved or explicitly excluded from prototype.

Summary: Document and validate existing solution architecture
Description:
Objective: Establish an evidence-backed architecture baseline and component responsibilities.

Detail: Document Unity Catalog, Delta layers, Python wheel, Job, notebooks, audit/rejects, and current deployment path.

Inputs: Repository implementation

Expected outputs: Current-state architecture
Acceptance Criteria:
- Current architecture matches databricks.yml, job YAML, source modules, and DDL.
- Trade/price parallel branches and join dependencies are accurate.
- Current provider, paused schedule, dev-only target, and notebook reporting are labelled as implemented/current limitations.

Summary: Approve target security and environment architecture
Description:
Objective: Define deployable dev/test/prod boundaries and least-privilege runtime identity.

Detail: Design only what is supported by actual workspace controls; confirm environment availability, principals, grants, networking, and secrets approach.

Inputs: Workspace/platform/security owner decisions

Expected outputs: Approved environment and access design
Acceptance Criteria:
- Environment promotion and job identity are approved by platform owner.
- Unity Catalog grants cover required schemas and Volume only; no secrets are committed.
- Architecture labels all unprovisioned targets and controls as proposed.

Summary: Confirm trade source contract and snapshot semantics
Description:
Objective: Make source ownership, completeness, corrections, and deletion semantics explicit.

Detail: Current input is synthetic; define the future producer contract and safe transition from full snapshot to an authoritative feed.

Inputs: Synthetic CSV; trade owner

Expected outputs: Trade source specification
Acceptance Criteria:
- Trade source owner, file schema, delivery cutoff, completeness marker, and correction/deletion semantics are recorded.
- A missing trade in a later snapshot is not treated as a cancellation without explicit business rule.
- Sample volume, retention, privacy classification, and replay window are approved or tracked as TBD.

Summary: Select and approve market-data source
Description:
Objective: Resolve whether Yahoo Finance is acceptable for the prototype and choose a licensed production source.

Detail: Confirm price type, currency, adjustments, symbol universe, rights, correction policy, availability, and missing-price escalation; synthetic fixtures are acceptable for deterministic tests only.

Inputs: Current yfinance adapter; market-data owner

Expected outputs: Approved source decision and interface contract
Acceptance Criteria:
- Provider and business owner approve data rights and use case before production.
- Price-date/price-type/currency contract and correction policy are documented.
- Daily availability and expected-session completeness thresholds have named owners.

Summary: Approve physical data dictionary and retention model
Description:
Objective: Review all current table grains, keys, financial types, lineage, and future retention needs.

Detail: Use the 10 physical DDL files as current-state truth; identify no enforced primary keys and no dedicated reference/reporting tables.

Inputs: database/tables DDL; provider/trade contracts

Expected outputs: Approved dictionary and data-retention decisions
Acceptance Criteria:
- Data dictionary lists every column and exact DDL type/nullability for all 10 tables.
- Business owner approves table grain and logical key assumptions.
- Partitioning/clustering remains absent unless measured query patterns justify it.
- Retention and Delta cleanup policy are approved before any production purge/optimization.

Summary: Maintain reproducible Databricks Asset Bundle development deployment
Description:
Objective: Validate current development Bundle build and deploy path.

Detail: Bundle builds a wheel and deploys the six-task job/notebooks to the dev target; schedule remains paused by configuration.

Inputs: databricks.yml; job resource; scripts/deploy.sh

Expected outputs: Validated dev deployment procedure
Acceptance Criteria:
- Bundle validation succeeds with the documented dev target and CLI profile.
- Wheel contains all six entry points and deploy uses repository source.
- Manual smoke run evidence is attached; no production readiness is inferred.

Summary: Add reviewed CI checks and controlled deployment promotion
Description:
Objective: Automate deterministic tests, Bundle validation, and reviewed artifact promotion.

Detail: Create CI using existing pytest/package/Bundle checks; add non-dev targets only after platform provisioning and identity approval.

Inputs: Approved environment/security design; current Bundle

Expected outputs: CI workflow and controlled deploy procedure
Acceptance Criteria:
- Pull request CI runs deterministic local tests and Bundle validation without credentials in logs.
- Deployment artifact/version is traceable to reviewed source revision.
- Promotion cannot unpause a schedule or deploy to an unapproved target without explicit approval.

Summary: Ingest synthetic trade snapshot into Bronze
Description:
Objective: Load structurally valid trade snapshots with deterministic raw lineage.

Detail: Current implementation validates the 14-field CSV and atomically overwrites Bronze after input checks.

Inputs: CSV snapshot in UC Volume

Expected outputs: cibc.bronze.trades
Acceptance Criteria:
- Exact schema, empty-file, and malformed-row cases are tested.
- Identical in-batch records are removed; versions of a trade remain present.
- Invalid file never overwrites existing Bronze; valid rerun yields same business rows.

Summary: Resolve trade snapshot disappearance and historical correction controls
Description:
Objective: Prevent a source snapshot replacement from leaving stale or silently deleting trades.

Detail: Current Bronze retains only latest snapshot and Silver does not remove trade IDs absent from a later file. Choose event/history storage or safe snapshot reconciliation.

Inputs: Approved trade source semantics; current Bronze/Silver behavior

Expected outputs: Versioned history/reconciliation design and tested implementation
Acceptance Criteria:
- Trade owner approves semantics for missing trade IDs, cancellation, and correction.
- A two-snapshot test proves accepted Silver matches the agreed authoritative source state.
- Backdated corrections are traceable and recompute the intended history without unrelated deletes.

Summary: Ingest and retain daily market-price history
Description:
Objective: Load supported daily close records with source identity and repeatable keys.

Detail: Current adapter calls Yahoo Finance, stores unadjusted closes, retries transient failures, and merges Bronze on symbol/date.

Inputs: Daily price provider response

Expected outputs: cibc.bronze.market_prices
Acceptance Criteria:
- Default symbols, date boundaries, provider response variants, NaN, duplicate keys, and retry errors have deterministic tests.
- Price rows carry source, currency, ingestion timestamp, and run lineage.
- Provider limitations and data rights are explicit in the source contract.

Summary: Harden price source decision and completeness exception process
Description:
Objective: Make price completeness and manual resolution operationally actionable.

Detail: Use provider choice from TMP-007; define approved synthetic fixtures for test environments and operational handling for late/missing prices.

Inputs: Approved provider decision; current completeness checks

Expected outputs: Price-source controls and exception runbook
Acceptance Criteria:
- Missing expected session is tied to symbol/date and owner; no stale price is used for position valuation.
- Test fixtures are deterministic and cannot be mistaken for production source data.
- Approved provider/credentials, rate limits, correction policy, and retries are configured outside source code where required.

Summary: Validate Silver trades and prices with reject history
Description:
Objective: Publish typed records only after business validation and deterministic version selection.

Detail: Current code performs typed conversion, configured business checks, deduplication/versioning, conditional merge, and reject-history writes.

Inputs: Bronze trades and prices

Expected outputs: Silver validated tables and rejects
Acceptance Criteria:
- Trade and price fixtures cover configured rules and reason codes.
- Silver trade business key is trade_id; price key is symbol + price_date.
- Reject writes are idempotent and preserve raw source fields/lineage; missing expected price blocks Silver update.

Summary: Run Spark/Delta integration and end-to-end rerun validation
Description:
Objective: Prove Delta writes, constraints, lineage, recovery, and same-input idempotency in a supported runtime.

Detail: Local Spark availability is not evidenced; docs/test_results.md records a successful dated pipeline run but its same-parameter second run was queued.

Inputs: Supported Spark/Delta environment; current test suite

Expected outputs: Integration, idempotency, and recovery evidence
Acceptance Criteria:
- Spark/Delta integration suite runs in a supported CI or Databricks test environment and results are retained.
- A second complete run with the same inputs verifies stable business keys/values and expected audit history growth.
- Failure injection confirms no unsafe publication and a documented rerun recovers the task.

Summary: Build cumulative daily positions and exact-date valuation
Description:
Objective: Publish historical positions at the agreed book/counterparty/instrument/date grain.

Detail: Current implementation aggregates signed trade quantities, carries positions across trading sessions, and joins same-day same-currency marks.

Inputs: Silver trades and prices

Expected outputs: cibc.gold.positions; position valuation breaks
Acceptance Criteria:
- Position grain and key match the approved dictionary.
- Daily buys, sells, net, closing quantity, close, and market value reconcile to independent calculations.
- Missing same-day price leaves price/value NULL and creates a break without changing quantity.

Summary: Calculate daily cash-equity mark-to-market P&L
Description:
Objective: Separate opening position market move from trade-day economic P&L.

Detail: Current Gold formula uses prior close for opening inventory and signed trade consideration for intraday activity; cumulative proxy is not true unrealized P&L.

Inputs: Gold positions; Silver trades/prices

Expected outputs: cibc.gold.daily_pnl; P&L breaks
Acceptance Criteria:
- Daily output grain is valuation_date + book_id + symbol + currency.
- Price movement and trade-day terms reconcile independently, including sells, new/flat positions, prior-close baseline, and missing prices.
- unrealized_pnl_proxy is clearly labelled as a cumulative proxy and is not presented as true unrealized P&L.

Summary: Provide notebook and SQL operational reporting
Description:
Objective: Expose current job run, audit metrics, rejections, positions, P&L, and valuation breaks.

Detail: A run-trigger notebook, read-only report notebook, and demo SQL exist. No deployed dashboard is evidenced.

Inputs: Gold/Silver tables and Jobs API

Expected outputs: Run-control/report notebooks and SQL queries
Acceptance Criteria:
- Run report identifies audit-derived status and clearly marks unavailable counts.
- Notebook output is read-only and totals reconcile to source tables.
- Report states that scheduled-run completeness is not evaluated and dashboard is not implemented.

Summary: Deliver user-accepted trading and P&L dashboard MVP
Description:
Objective: Present agreed Gold reporting datasets in an approved Databricks SQL dashboard or chosen BI tool.

Detail: Dashboard technology, user roles, filters, reconciliation views, and access model remain to be confirmed; this is proposed work, not current functionality.

Inputs: Approved reporting requirements; Gold datasets

Expected outputs: Dashboard MVP and validation evidence
Acceptance Criteria:
- Product owner signs off audience, filters, date/book/symbol dimensions, and exception drill-through.
- Dashboard totals reconcile to Gold daily_pnl and positions for agreed test dates.
- Dashboard access is least privilege and deployment is repeatable; no dashboard is reported as live before sign-off.

Summary: Maintain deterministic unit and transformation tests
Description:
Objective: Protect module contracts and calculation rules with repeatable test cases.

Detail: Tests cover source parsing, transformations, DDL/query shape, packaging, notebook helpers, and financial examples; Spark-dependent cases need a compatible runtime. Three focused tests currently fail because they reference removed Silver *_constraints.sql files; current checks are consolidated into trades.sql and market_prices.sql.

Inputs: pytest suite; supported Python/Spark runtime

Expected outputs: Deterministic test evidence
Acceptance Criteria:
- Business-rule tests include correction, duplicate, calendar, missing price, short position, and P&L decomposition cases.
- CI reports skips separately from passes and does not treat unavailable Spark tests as verified.
- Replace stale test references with the consolidated Silver DDL and verify its CHECK constraints.
- New failures are triaged against the baseline; no unrelated failures are silently waived.

Summary: Complete independent position/P&L reconciliation and UAT
Description:
Objective: Close the gap between pipeline output and business-approved calculations.

Detail: The 2026-10-11 run has independent SQL reconciliation with zero reported mismatches; same-input rerun remained queued in the report.

Inputs: Gold outputs; independent SQL; business test cases

Expected outputs: Reconciliation and UAT sign-off
Acceptance Criteria:
- Trade-to-position quantities reconcile by date/book/counterparty/instrument.
- Position market value and daily P&L reconcile using approved close/baseline/trade cash-flow methodology.
- Business owner signs UAT evidence for representative long, short, flat, correction, and missing-price cases.
- A complete same-input rerun has recorded evidence; do not rely only on unit tests.

Summary: Operate the dev workflow with controlled scheduling
Description:
Objective: Use existing Asset Bundle workflow safely and keep schedule gated on readiness.

Detail: Current Job allows one concurrent run, runs six tasks, and has a weekday 18:00 America/New_York schedule configured as PAUSED.

Inputs: Deployed dev Job; operational readiness decisions

Expected outputs: Controlled dev operating procedure
Acceptance Criteria:
- Manual run and failure states are visible in Job UI and audit tables.
- Schedule remains paused until source owner, support contact, permissions, runbook, and alert path are approved.
- Any future unpause/change is reviewed and recorded with owner and rollback path.

Summary: Create support runbook, alerting, and handover
Description:
Objective: Prepare an operational handoff with actionable diagnosis and escalation.

Detail: Define monitoring on Job/audit/reject/break signals; alerting and support ownership are not implemented in the repo.

Inputs: Approved NFRs; report; reconciliation; support contacts

Expected outputs: Runbook, notification path, handover sign-off
Acceptance Criteria:
- Runbook describes failed task diagnosis, source repair, safe rerun, reconciliation, and escalation owner.
- Alert criteria and response targets are approved and tested; proposed five-minute detection target remains proposed until measured.
- Handover includes architecture, data contracts, access, known limitations, deployment procedure, and open risks.
